title: What is the appeal of movies like Tár?

commenti.body: I don’t understand how you can look at a film like Tár, which despite being quite long is so precise in its storytelling that I think it’s a marvel of a movie, and just conclude that it’s “dull conversation”. Every scene and every conversation reveals so much about Tár, about the people around her, and gradually outlines the themes of the story. In terms of drama films, this one was very exhilarating IMO.
Yeah, I can't agree with you on this one. I watched it on a plane and was riveted. Every scene built on the last and the tension as her house of cards began to collapse was really effective for me.

The insistence I’ve seen in so many online discussions that films need to be entertaining is so strange to me. I mean, it’s so reductive to attach to films as their only merit that they have to be entertaining. Completely disregarding the fact that entertaining is such a broad term as to border on the meaningless (it can mean many things for many different people), I still can’t wrap my head around why people can’t appreciate that there is more to filmmaking than just mere entertainment. Some people actually like to be challenged by art, exposed to new ideas, put to reflect on their own experiences and how those relate to the world at large - even if that process is not „entertaining“ in the moment and may require a certain investment and trust into the film that could be described, in a derogative way, as a „chore“. If you don’t find anything of value for ourselves in that, that’s totally fine, but the way this post is framing this subject just screams ignorance.

>Reading reviews/analyses/essays on films you don't understand can help you develop an appreciation. Understaning what the movie is about is the first step toward enjoying it.

>​

>Why is Tár entertaining? For one, that's extremely subjective. I personally find Tár to be very  entertaining, I could watch that film back-to-back even before untangling all its metaphors. It's fine if you find a movie boring, it happens. The type of story Tár is trying to tell calls for subtlety. It wouldn't be the same film if the dramatic conflict were more obvious.

Like I already mentioned, I don't mind reading articles or listening to discussions explaining movies that I didn't understand. But I'm only gonna do that if the movie actually sticks in my mind and gives me motivation to go out and understand it more. Like I mentioned, The Lighthouse is a perfect example. I didn't understand much of it, but the movie is so captivating and scary it made me WANT to understand better later on, it stuck in my memory. Tár doesn't give me any of that. Aside from Cate Blanchett's performance i found myself just thinking "ok what's the significance of this scene" or "ok this scene is trying to convey something deeper" instead of the movie getting me to care about any of the characters. I felt like I was watching the movie just for the sake of it and going out and reading interpretations just to understand some of it feels like doing a homework assignment more than anything else.

When did I say that a movie's only purpose is to be entertaining? I just said that a movie should be sufficiently entertaining/interesting/capitivating/engaging in order for me to care about the themes and ideas conveyed in the movie. I don't think anything I've said warrants calling me ignorant.

In fairness I was kind of throwing you under the bus for the trend in general of people complaining when films don’t entertain them that I’ve come across a lot in online discussions about film. And I’ve actually seen people literally claim a movie‘s only purpose is to be entertaining - so I’m perhaps just a bit sensitive. And while you apparently use words like entertaining, interesting or captivating interchangeably, I would argue that these qualities can but don’t necessarily have to mean the same thing. There is a whole world of cinema out there, like slow cinema for example, that has nothing to do with traditional notions of entertainment but can be as (or even more) arresting and thought provoking as the best that main stream cinema has to offer. That’s what I mean when I talk about ignorance - it was perhaps a unnecessarily harsh way to put it, but I wanted to point out that to understand the appeal of those types of films, it would help to broaden your horizons on what cinema can be.
